unit.title: Angles and Movement
unit.blurb: Turns as angles, right angles and quarter, half and whole turns, compass directions, and describing position and movement on a grid.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Recognise angles as turns, including right angles, and compare angles with a right angle.

O2.t: Use compass directions and describe position and movement on a grid.

p: An **angle** is an amount of turn. A **quarter turn** is a **right angle**. Two quarter turns make a **half turn**; four make a **whole turn**.
Angles smaller than a right angle are **acute**; bigger ones (less than a half turn) are **obtuse**.

lesson.t: Why a right angle is a quarter turn
p: A full turn goes all the way round. Two right angles make a half turn and four make a full turn, so a right angle is a quarter turn.

lesson.q: You face north and turn clockwise through 2 right angles. Which way do you face?

p: Say which way: clockwise or anticlockwise.
Clockwise means turning the same way as clock hands.

p: The four **compass directions** are North, East, South and West.
To describe movement on a grid say how many squares and which way: '3 squares East, then 2 squares North'.

lesson.t: Why we give directions in order
p: A route only works if the moves are in the right order. Each move starts from where the last one finished.

lesson.q: Start at (1, 1). Move 3 squares right, then 2 squares up. Where are you?

p: Do each move in order: count squares carefully.
Count the jumps from one square to the next.
